The original workaround is to write matching settings with MWB closed.

The same commenter reports a 22-character entry truncated to 16 characters with different magic numbers; truncation and persistence must not be assumed to be the same defect.

fix_assessment.rationale: Open PR #51377 implements and adds tests for the key-edit persistence path described in #27945. Current main's frmMatrix.UpdateKey changes only Encryption.MyKey, while the reload path can adopt the persisted key. This concrete attempt strongly matches the manual-file workaround, but does not establish that all invalid-key symptoms or long-key truncation are resolved.

issue_context.summary: MWB rejects keys entered through its UI while stopped-process file edits work. A new 0.102.2862.0 report adds differing magic numbers and truncation observations. An existing PR addresses typed-key persistence, so it should be tested rather than replaced by another fix plan.
known_information: The original version is 0.101.2362.0 installed with WinGet; attempts included simple 16-character manual keys, so special-character escaping alone does not explain all attempts.
The October 17 commenter reports the same failure on 0.102.2862.0 with both per-user and machine-wide installs.
Both reports say stopped-process manual settings edits restore connection.
A maintainer requested /bugreport and /reportbug in August; no ZIP has since been attached, but a new commenter supplied substantive behavior evidence.
The issue remains open and unassigned, with four comments and no Needs-Author-Feedback label.
PR #51377 is open and non-draft; #27945's latest comment explicitly explains the stored/live-key divergence it addresses.
inferences: Typed-key persistence is a substantially better-grounded explanation than attributing every failure to arbitrary concurrent-file access.
The new report predates any merge of #51377; it is not evidence that the PR has failed.
The overview in #51077 also flags protocol-version mismatch as an alternative. Both peers' exact versions are not established, so that alternative is not disproved.
The 22-to-16-character truncation observation may be a separate UI behavior; no independent correction is proposed from that observation alone.

reproduce.title: Compare MWB typed-key persistence before and after the existing fix
reproduce.version_requirement: Use identical PowerToys versions on both peers. Start with reported 0.102.2862.0 or 0.101.2362.0, then compare an isolated development build of PR #51377.
prerequisites: Two Windows test machines with MWB enabled and a working permitted network connection.
Use disposable test settings and preserve the original configuration.
Use a non-sensitive synthetic key; never publish actual pairing keys or complete settings files.
setup: Ensure both peers use the same exact build and record installation scope.
Prepare two distinct valid synthetic 16-character keys and identify the legacy MWB matrix form separately from PowerToys Settings.
steps: 1. Establish a baseline connection using a known test key.
2. In the MWB matrix form, enter the same different valid test key on both peers and apply the change.
3. Check whether connection and displayed magic-number agreement reflect the edited key; reopen the form and restart MWB to force persistence/reload.
4. If the key reverts, compare with the reported workaround: fully exit PowerToys on both machines, apply the same test key to the relevant settings, then restart. Do not edit live settings.
5. Repeat the UI-edit/reload test in an isolated build of existing PR #51377 and run its key-persistence/invalid-input tests.
6. Separately record whether a 22-character entry is truncated and whether the two settings surfaces behave differently. Do not treat this as proof of the persistence defect.
reproduce.expected_result: An accepted UI key edit survives reload and restart and produces matching peer state. Rejected input leaves both stored and runtime keys unchanged. Any remaining failure is separated from mismatched versions or long-key truncation.
